 Pakistan looks to close out an unbeaten round-robin stage on Tuesday while Sri Lanka can earn a berth in Saturday’s final with a win in the Tri-Nations ODI Series.
 Pakistan (3-0) escaped trouble again on Sunday, clinching a berth in the Saturday’s Tri-Nations One-Day International Series final, and the Shaheens can complete an unbeaten run through round-robin play on Tuesday when the play Sri Lanka (1-1) at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, Pakistan. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, comes off the second-highest chase in ODI history on Thursday and can clinch a spot opposite the Shaheens in the final with a victory. A win by Pakistan keeps 0-3 England alive for a spot in the final as it closes out the round-robin phase on Thursday against Sri Lanka.

 Pakistan rang up 89 runs for the 10th wicket, a record in a successful ODI chase, to score a one-wicket win on Sunday over England, 243/9-241. Shabab Khan put up 113 not out (96) to carry the Shaheens to the win, with Saad Baig the next most-productive batter with a modest 32 (22). Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi bowled 4/46 while Razaullah and Arafat Minhas took two wickets each.
 On Thursday in Rawalpindi, Sri Lanka faced a huge uphill climb and pulled it off when Janith Liyanage blasted a 6 on the next-to-last ball of the match to lift it to a remarkable two-wicket victory, 430/8-429/4. Pavan Rathnayake powered the chase with 130 (106) while Aviskha Fernando went for 97 (83) and Dasun Shanaka got 97 (50) with eight 6s. The bowlers took just four wickets, with Dunith Wellalage getting a 2/56 performance while Harry Brook’s 202 (116), England’s first-ever ODI double century, went for naught.
 The Shaheens opened the series on Oct. 18 with a 37-run win over Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and enter Tuesday’s match with four consecutive wins.
